t: Binary Searchable Numbers in an Unsorted Array — Values No Pivot Choice Can Discard
o: The randomized search maintains a window that initially spans the whole array; whenever pivot < target it deletes the pivot and everything left of it, and whenever pivot > target it deletes the pivot and everything right of it. A value counts only if it survives every conceivable sequence of pivot choices. Take Example 3, nums = [2,1,3,5,4], whose answer is 3: value 3 always survives because everything left of it is smaller (such pivots delete leftward, keeping 3) and everything right of it is larger (such pivots delete rightward); value 2 dies instantly if the adversary picks 1 as the first pivot, and value 5 dies if the adversary picks 4. Uniqueness of elements matters — with duplicates the guarantee itself becomes ill-defined. This characterization decomposes into independent left/right scans, so after an O(n^2) brute force there is a clean linear solution built on prefix maxima and suffix minima.
k: nums[i] is guaranteed found iff every element to its left is smaller AND every element to its right is larger than nums[i].
Sufficiency: under those conditions any chosen pivot points away from index i correctly, so the window keeps containing i until the pivot IS nums[i].
Necessity: a single violating neighbor is a legal pivot choice whose deletion direction wipes out index i on the very first step.

a.i: Directly translate the characterization: for each index scan everything to its left looking for a greater value and everything to its right looking for a smaller value. Any hit disqualifies the index; count the survivors.
s: For each index i assume searchable.
Scan j < i; if any nums[j] > nums[i], disqualify i.
Scan k > i; if any nums[k] < nums[i], disqualify i.
Count indices that were never disqualified.
a.t: O(n^2) — two linear scans per element

a.n: Approach 2: Prefix Maxima and Suffix Minima
a.i: Both checks only ever consult the maximum to the left and the minimum to the right, so precompute prefMax[i] = max(nums[0..i-1]) and sufMin[i] = min(nums[i+1..n-1]) in two passes. Index i qualifies exactly when prefMax[i] < nums[i] < sufMin[i], with infinities serving as sentinels at the two ends.
s: Build prefMax left to right with sentinel -infinity.
Build sufMin right to left with sentinel +infinity.
Count indices i satisfying prefMax[i] < nums[i] < sufMin[i].

w: Lead with the adversarial-pivot argument before writing any code — interviewers grade the characterization, not the implementation. Pitfalls: forgetting the sentinel values at the boundary indices, silently assuming the array is sorted (it need not be), and ignoring that uniqueness of elements underpins the whole guarantee. A strictly increasing array makes all n values searchable while a strictly decreasing one makes none. Follow-up: report the guaranteed values themselves, or adapt the criterion when duplicates are allowed (e.g., only counting strict violations).
